As the new school year begins, an increasing number of Americans are expressing support for students being banned from using their phones throughout the entire school day.

With the start of the new school year, voices supporting a phone ban in classrooms continue to grow

Yes, it's still July, but somehow summer is already over. My kids go back to school today and tomorrow — this is the second summer in a row where school has started before August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual 'Back to School' promotion: eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27 will receive a gift card of up to $150 in value. Consumers in several U.S. states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

Although back-to-school discounts are very popular, the use of smartphones during class time is increasingly no longer tolerated.

The most upvoted comment was posted by bibliophilecode

As a high school student, when the phone ban was implemented last year, I had only one thought — the ban needs to be tightened further. The ban we have during class time (excluding lunch and study halls) is sometimes ignored by both teachers and students, but when it is followed, the results are very significant. I can't count how many people's grades slipped because they were playing games during class instead of paying attention.

A new survey by the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% of people currently oppose classroom bans.

Support for a stricter, all-day ban from the first bell to the last bell has risen even faster. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose banning phone use for the entire school day.

The survey also noted that while support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger adults are still less enthusiastic about classroom bans and all-day bans. Click here to read the full report.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only during class, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
